# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Runs `solo` (one agent implements both features) on the 50-pair `flash` subset with the same setup as the `low` and `high` thinking runs (`gemini-3.8-flash`, 500 steps, compaction at 64K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap), changing only the thinking level to `medium`. It completes the `low` / `medium` / `high` comparison for `solo` and is the `solo` reference for [`coop --git` at `medium`](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium/summary.md) (38/50). It ran as two 25-pair halves on two API keys and was merged into this one run.

## Observations

- 33/50 (66%). Thinking level barely changes `solo` on these pairs: 36/50 and 32/50 at `low` (two runs), 33/50 at `medium`, and 34/50 at `high`, all within the 4 to 6 pair run-to-run variation.
- Two agents beat one at `medium`: `coop --git` scored 38/50 with the same settings, and pair by pair 5 pairs passed only in `coop --git` while none passed only in `solo` (exact two-sided test, p = 0.06). The five were `huggingface_datasets_task/3997` (2,4), `pallets_click_task/2068` (5,11), `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), `pallets_jinja_task/1559` (4,8), and `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (3,7).
- A single agent carrying both features works longer and compacts more than each `coop` agent: median 133 steps and 5 compactions per agent (vs. 92 steps and 2 compactions for `coop --git` at `medium`), and 3 agents reached the 500-step limit.
- Cost `$82.07` (`$1.64` per pair), about the same as `coop --git` at `medium` (`$81.68`), roughly three times `solo` at `low` (`$25.70`), and below `solo` at `high` (`$110.14`).
